title: Platform event envelope
description: Every event accepted by the shared core carries this envelope, whether it arrives from an inbound webhook, a probe, an application or an internal scheduler. Producers choose eventID; consumers treat (source, eventID) as the idempotency key, so a retried delivery is a duplicate rather than a second business fact. Time is producer-claimed and bounded by maxClockSkewSeconds at ingestion; the core stores its own receipt time separately.

eventID.description: Producer-assigned unique id. Opaque to the core; only equality matters.

source.description: Authenticated producer identity, also the idempotency namespace. The core never trusts a client-supplied source to differ from the authenticated principal.

time.description: Producer-claimed occurrence time, RFC 3339 with an explicit offset.

type.description: Dotted event type, stable per producer contract.

service.description: Service the event is about, not the transport that carried it.

traceID.description: W3C trace id, 32 lowercase hex characters. Present when the producer is part of a trace.

spanID.description: W3C span id, 16 lowercase hex characters. Only meaningful together with traceID.

attributes.description: Flattened, already-redacted string map. Values are strings so a single redaction pass covers every producer; nested or binary payloads are forbidden.

dedupeKey.description: Optional explicit idempotency key for producers whose natural key is not eventID alone, for example a repeated webhook delivery id. When present it, not eventID, decides the duplicate.

allOf.description: A span id without a trace id cannot be correlated, so it is rejected rather than stored uselessly.
